clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute transverse myelitis (ATM) in the context of recent COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man presented with progressive bilateral lower limb weakness, urinary retention, and constipation following recent COVID-19 infection confirmed by PCR. Neurological exam revealed upper motor neuron signs in the lower limbs. MRI spine with contrast demonstrated a long segment central T2 hyperintense lesion from T7 to T10 without enhancement or mass, consistent with spinal cord inflammation. CSF analysis showed elevated protein with normal glucose, negative bacterial cultures, and negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR. MRI brain and orbits were negative for inflammatory changes, excluding cerebral demyelination. SARS-CoV-2 serology confirmed recent infection with positive IgG, IgA, and IgM. No CSF oligoclonal bands result was reported. Clinical course and treatment details were not documented in the source. The combined clinical presentation, imaging, CSF findings, and serology support the diagnosis of acute transverse myelitis triggered by recent COVID-19 infection.
